stories.event: The special European Council on the 2028–34 budget (MFF) and Ukraine financing for 2027 continues in Brussels on Friday 27 November and is due to end that day; Costa says he will share his conclusions on Friday. The Commission proposed €45bn of EU-borrowed financing for Ukraine in 2027 (€20bn budget support, €25bn military) on 18 November; it needs a unanimous amendment of the MFF regulation. Czechia, Slovakia and Hungary refuse to take part; Merz ties Germany's yes to the MFF to all 27 sharing Ukraine costs; ambassadors' notes of 24 November see the end of 2026 as the consensus deadline. Babiš comments to Czech media in Brussels.

claims.label: Ukraine loan agreed at the summit
claims.text: EU leaders at the special European Council in Brussels, which is due to end on Friday 27 November 2026, agree to provide Ukraine with €45bn of EU-borrowed financing for 2027 (the Commission's proposed loan), whether or not all 27 member states take part.
claims.criterion: YES if, between 10:00 on Thu 26 Nov and 23:59 on Fri 27 Nov 2026 (Europe/Brussels), the European Council agrees to provide Ukraine with financing for 2027 of at least €45bn based on EU borrowing (the Commission's Coordinated Support Facility for Ukraine / top-up of the Ukraine Support Loan, or a changed structure that leaders say is that financing), in any configuration (all 27; some member states not contributing, contributing only to the civilian part, or opting out through enhanced cooperation). Any of these counts: (a) European Council conclusions or another European Council text published on consilium.europa.eu, including a text "firmly supported by" fewer than 27 heads of state or government, with wording such as "agrees to provide", "agrees on" or "endorses the Commission's proposal … and calls for its swift adoption"; (b) António Costa saying at the closing press conference or on X that leaders agreed it; (c) at least two of AFP, Reuters, AP, Bloomberg, Euronews, ČTK or Ukrinform reporting, citing Costa, leaders or officials, that leaders agreed it. NO if, by 23:59 Fri 27 Nov, leaders only "take note", "will revert", hand the file to ministers or the December European Council, agree only on principles, or agree on less than €45bn for 2027; NO also if the agreement is first announced after 23:59 Fri (summit running into Saturday). Reports published later about an agreement announced in the window count.

cs.criterion: ANO, pokud se Evropská rada mezi 10:00 ve čtvrtek 26. listopadu a 23:59 v pátek 27. listopadu 2026 (bruselského času) dohodne poskytnout Ukrajině na rok 2027 financování ve výši nejméně 45 miliard eur založené na výpůjčkách EU (návrh Komise nebo změněná struktura, o níž lídři řeknou, že jde o toto financování), v jakémkoli složení (všech 27 států, některé státy bez příspěvku, jen civilní část nebo posílená spolupráce). Rozhoduje (a) text Evropské rady na consilium.europa.eu, včetně textu „pevně podpořeného“ méně než 27 lídry, se slovy jako „souhlasí s poskytnutím“, „dohodla se“ nebo „podporuje návrh Komise … a vyzývá k jeho rychlému přijetí“; (b) prohlášení Antónia Costy na závěrečné tiskové konferenci nebo na síti X; nebo (c) zprávy nejméně dvou z agentur a médií AFP, Reuters, AP, Bloomberg, Euronews, ČTK nebo Ukrinform s odvoláním na představitele EU. NE, pokud lídři věc jen vezmou na vědomí, odloží ji, předají ministrům nebo prosincové Evropské radě, shodnou se jen na zásadách nebo na méně než 45 miliardách eur, anebo pokud je dohoda poprvé oznámena až po 23:59 v pátek.

research.question: Friday 27 Nov third-reading block (print 311 first, 270 second, 213 third, 47 fourth): until when does the sitting run, any plan to extend, any announced opposition obstruction, and how did the 6 Nov Friday fail?
research.finding: End time: third readings on a Friday may run only until 14:00. ČT24, 3 Jul 2026 (a Friday): 'Ve 14:00 uplynula vyměřená doba, do níž může sněmovna zákony ve třetím čtení projednávat'. The building-law third reading broke off at that point and was carried over to a later day. No coalition motion or plan to extend Friday 27 Nov past 14:00 was found. This week's only extension was the Wednesday vote to sit past 21:00 for the budget second reading (ČT24 live, 25 Nov). Extending Friday would need a plenary vote at the start of the day. Obstruction: no opposition announcement of obstruction aimed at Friday or at prints 311 or 213 was found (searches up to 25 Nov evening; latest opposition statements on lex Orlen date from 13 Nov). Pattern this week: on Tue 24 Nov the opposition stretched the agenda debate (programme approved after about 6 hours, 40 change proposals, breaks after 23:00). On Wed 25 Nov morning, though, the third-reading block moved fast: print 48 passed 11:36 and print 210 at 11:58, after five agenda votes 09:06-09:34 (ČT24 tema page; dossier snapshot). How 6 Nov failed: that Friday had no fixed third-reading slots. The time went on the pension-savings second reading (passed on the fourth attempt, almost 50 amendments read in) and a roughly 30-minute power cut that halted the sitting in the morning. The 34th sitting was then closed with lex Ukrajina, the NKÚ amendment and the groundwater fee postponed. The opposition had promised a thorough debate of every bill over the Okamura dispute; the coalition had only dropped night sittings (ČT24 6 Nov). Rules: a July 2026 anti-obstruction amendment to the Rules of Procedure limits speakers on agenda-change motions and lets the plenary cap speaking time on bills. Whether it is in force was not checked. The 14:00 cut-off fits with print 311 running from 09:00 (2 registered speakers). Print 213 comes after the pension bill (print 270, slot contested 97-36), so it carries the timing risk.

research.question: On the preliminary party vote, how close is the last NZ First / ACT list seat under Sainte-Laguë (who holds the 120th quotient, who is next, what shift moves it), how does that compare with special-vote shifts in 2017/2020/2023, and what exactly do the published analyses (The Overhang, Kiwiblog, Lee, Westpac) say?
research.finding: Recomputing Sainte-Laguë from the preliminary shares (Lab 710,330 / Nat 706,680 votes; Grn 13.30, ACT 10.92, NZF 9.78, TOP 5.96, TPM 0.57 %; about 2.419M valid party votes) reproduces the official 120-seat split (Lab 36, Nat 35, Grn 16, ACT 13, NZF 12, TOP 7, TPM 1). Labour holds the 120th quotient (Lab/71 = 10,005), National is next (Nat/71 = 9,953). NZ First's 12th seat is the 118th quotient (10,288). With everything else unchanged, NZ First keeps it only if it loses fewer than about 7,700 votes (0.32 points of the preliminary total). Put another way, it needs at least about 7.5–8.75% of the 345–400k special votes, against 9.78% on election night, so roughly 76–89% of its preliminary share. In 2017 NZ First won only about 75% of its preliminary share among specials (7.51% → 7.20% overall), and Chuan-Zheng Lee's mechanical projections, which replay the 2017, 2020 and 2023 special-vote patterns, have NZ First losing one seat in all three. ACT is not close: it has about 15,400 votes of cushion (0.64 points). So one NZ First list-seat loss is the expected case on every historical pattern, not an outside chance. A path the forecasters' framing leaves out: if National also loses a party-vote entitlement (35→34), its overhang grows and the House becomes 132, so NZ First −1 alone gives 66/132, an exact tie and therefore NO, even if no electorate flips. That is Lee's 2020-pattern projection, and Farrar's net −3 arithmetic says the same. The published analyses are dated model outputs, not results. The Overhang (17 Nov) puts NZ First losing a seat at 97% and National losing an entitlement at 66%. Lee (8 and 16 Nov) has NZ First −1 in all three replays and the bloc on 66/131 only on the 2023 pattern. Farrar (Kiwiblog, 26 Nov NZDT) calls an NZ First list loss and a Wairarapa flip 'likely'. Westpac (9 Nov) expects the right bloc to fall short without Opportunity.

cs.text: Rychlý odhad INE zveřejněný v pátek 27. listopadu 2026 v 9:00 SEČ ukáže meziroční růst spotřebitelských cen (CPI) ve Španělsku v listopadu 2026 ve výši …
cs.criterion: Hodnota je meziroční míra celkového indexu spotřebitelských cen (IPC general, Španělsko) za listopad 2026 na jedno desetinné místo, jak ji uvede rychlý odhad INE (indicador adelantado del IPC/IPCA, noviembre 2026) zveřejněný 27. listopadu 2026 (madridského času). HICP, jádrová inflace, meziměsíční změna ani definitivní listopadová data (polovina prosince) nerozhodují. Pokud INE rychlý odhad 27. listopadu 2026 nezveřejní, tvrzení propadá (bez hodnoty).

forecast.scale_source: RMS of (actual − consensus) over 14 Spanish flash CPI releases on the Nasdaq economic calendar (data/dossiers/2026-11-28/es-cpi-28.md)
forecast.consensus_note: The five centre about 0.12 pp below a consensus that only repeats October's 4.9% (0.6 scale), for a documented reason: Spanish petrol is down 16.3% since end-September to €1.624/l in the EU Oil Bulletin after seven weekly falls (dossier), against a base month (November 2025) of +0.2% m/m.
